description: Canonical registry of conformance vector identifiers. Every ak.vector.* identifier referenced by prose or fixtures MUST appear here, and every row MUST point at the prose or fixture source that defines it.

vectors.description: Authority-pair uniqueness, signed Event principal_server_id, exact producer-proof binding, origin-only admission and replica preservation.

The Realm ak.realm.policy_bundle aad_visibility.event_id component is a disclosure ceiling over the encrypted-envelope aad_visibility_event_id discriminator: an equal or narrower envelope is accepted, a wider one is rejected with aad_visibility_policy_violation, and an absent component means the hidden ceiling rather than no constraint.
Personal blocklist whole-value CAS updates, target closure, shared-history receive-before-filter behavior, unblock projection rebuild and non-enumerable holder-side filtering.

Account Data keys are server-versioned compare-and-set registers: a stale byte-identical retry after a newer write is rejected with cas_conflict, concurrent delete/update elects exactly one winner, opposite arrival orders reach the same final state, the revision high-water mark survives tombstone GC so deleted values cannot be resurrected, and value_tombstone key patterns refuse physical delete.

A human Contact petname is globally keyed by peer.principal_id through an opaque holder-private HMAC/JCS suffix; raw principal IDs, Realm IDs, pairwise actor IDs, and peer service IDs are forbidden key material, and decrypted slot swapping fails closed.

The two registered typed-id account-data namespaces are closed: ak.views.private.<view_id> and ak.notifications.inbox.<notification_id> accept only a full typed id tail, reject the bare namespace instead of falling through to the permissive unregistered-key branch, refuse plaintext content, bind the decrypted private View to visibility=private and its own view_id while the shared ak.view.* surfaces reject visibility=private, close the inbox value to dismissed/archived with an HLC-then-device_id merge, and delete physically without allowing revival.
Account Authority evidence, PCR-scoped ak.account.status publication, idempotent pending-to-accepted operation state and bounded Principal Server fanout.

Actor Profile accountability admission is deterministic: every declared principal needs an active matching grant, any missing grant rejects the whole Event, and field-stripped acceptance is non-conformant.
Actor-chain sequence and sibling buckets are Realm-scoped; cross-Realm equal sequence values are independent, while same-Realm conflicting siblings fork and cross-Realm predecessor references fail.
Realm-scoped actor frontiers bind realm_id and actor_id, start at actor_seq 0, retain the complete sorted sibling head set, and hash the closed realm_actor transcript deterministically.
Byte-level MLS-Exporter KAT for arkret-aead-sender-nonce-prefix-v1, including the exact JCS context, AES-GCM prefix length, counter concatenation, and context-field negative mutations.

Controller-owned recovery_public_key backup of managed Agent PCR MLS state, canonical managed-principal binding across public/plaintext/AAD views, pairing recovery-readiness gate, and prohibition on Agent runtime private-key backup or per-Agent human mnemonic.
Managed-agent DID-to-PCR binding, controller delegated authoring attribution, control-fact placement, and rejection of non-PCR Realms at either principal control id.

Native Agent MLS KeyPackages bind exclusively to the current accepted ak.agent.key.authorize Event and its runtime signing key, never to a controller delegated-device authorization; stale, mixed, cross-principal, revoked, superseded, expired, or key-mismatched bindings fail closed.

Managed Agent bootstrap is constructed in one acyclic order: controller-signed PCR-independent DID entry 0 -> exact initial_resolution -> frozen genesis create -> realm_id=retype(event_id) -> accepted provision -> accepted PCR -> controller-signed create-locked DID entry 1. Covers awaiting_pcr_genesis and awaiting_did_binding invisibility, exact durable commitment comparison, activation only after entry 1, and rejection of same-batch submission, undeclared genesis, duplicate claim, service-chosen realm id, cross-server split or wrong DID update key/tuple.

Explicit two-step abandonment of an accepted ak.agent.provision whose managed Agent PCR genesis will never arrive: a single-use challenge pins the agent, slug, declared realm id and allocation, and one transaction consumes it, releases both claims and records exactly one tombstone. Covers slug reuse after release, the permanently unusable realm-id claim, replay returning one terminal outcome, and rejection without a challenge, with replayed credentials, after expiry, after consumption, and once the genesis is accepted.

Provision requested_scope is a required immutable global ceiling rather than a grant; narrower key scopes and Realm grants are accepted, while action/resource/mandatory-constraint widening fails closed and provisioning emits no Realm grant.

The public managed-Agent DID history contains only the requested_scope commitment digest; complete scope disclosure is controller-signed, verifier/audience/challenge-bound, short-window private evidence, and public-copy, mismatch, stale, wrong-audience, and replay variants fail closed.
Stable runtime key binding digest, same-binding idempotent retry, different-binding HTTP 409 conflict, and stale approval fail-closed behavior.

Executes the portable Agent signer evidence transcript across exact-request current admission, destination-receipted historical verification, three orthogonal lifecycle gates, canonical witnesses, MLS cross-binding and tamper cases.

High-risk agent session scope returns claim_required with closed details {reason_code=human_approval_required, approval_request_id}; controller approval is out of band and CAPTCHA, OTP, password, and browser challenges are forbidden on the runtime path.
Request-key canonical body conflict, scope binding, canonical_hash_input and 24-hour retention semantics.

Deterministic Applet registration_epoch recomputation from the closed normalized transcript, UTF-8 domain separator, JCS bytes, and SHA-256; covers set sorting and duplicate rejection, optional omission, DID method version evidence, and security-field rotation.

Caller-signed Applet revoke plan binding, durable pre-effect ledger bound to principal service and admin actor, exact replay, conflict rejection, non-skip partial outcomes, restart recovery, and first-accepted-event write fencing.

Applet transaction push delivery authentication record: per-delivery RFC 9421 HTTP Message Signature covering method/target/authority/content-digest/source-service-id/destination-service-id/idempotency-key, receiver-derived delivery_authentication_record and its domain-separated digest are persisted into the idempotency/replay record, duplicate body/record conflicts fail closed, and source service authentication does not replace Event actor/applet/capability checks.
Release requires an active binding, unexpired authorization, and accepted session head notice; suspended, revoked, expired, or wrong-stage inputs fail closed.
Audit binding is a closed control-plane FSM: active and suspended may transition as registered, revoked is terminal, and same-basis conflicting siblings produce Bottom.
Same-basis close dominates release, earlier accepted releases must be frozen in close release_refs, post-close releases fail, and ordered_log ordering is deterministic.
Release recipient actor and public key must exactly match authorization and resolve to the same authorized audit actor; substitution fails closed.
Release is bounded by binding activation, first_auditable_epoch, encryption-time eligibility, sealed epoch state, and sealed_by_commit_ref.
Release material output is gated on accepted release plus a profile-valid RYW receipt, matching policy digest, and independent witnesses where attested hardware is claimed.
Audit session stages follow the registered request-authorize-notice-close FSM, permit explicit early close, reject skipped stages, and make close terminal.
field_access.sensitive_fields read projection handling: redact/hash/omit remove original values, hash uses keyed/salted digest discipline, and unenforceable handling falls back to omit.
Closed SessionGrant issuance preimage, typed ID/JWT jti derivation, holder/recovery binding, canonical public-JWK normalization, durable exact replay, conflict and terminal outcomes.
Authority lease issuance, ordered batch delivery, exact idempotent refresh, founding anchor basis, stale/quorum failure and cache-clearing boundaries.

Executable closed WebSocket discovery and frame bytes, application-context DPoP KAT and replay binding, account/events/signal multiplex isolation, duplicate/unknown/oversize negatives, reauth, drain, close-code traces and mandatory HTTP fallback.

Streaming AEAD declared-bounds negatives (declared fields only, no multi-MiB payload materialised): segment_count above 2^20, segment_bytes below 1 KiB or above 8 MiB, and segment_count inconsistent with ceil(size_bytes / segment_bytes) MUST all be rejected fail-closed (schema_violation, reason_code segment_bounds_invalid) before key derivation or any segment download.
Streaming AEAD ordering: out-of-order / skipped / gapped segment_index MUST be rejected with segment_sequence_invalid; a repeated segment_index MUST be rejected with segment_replay.

Streaming chunked AEAD (ak.blob.stream_aead.v1) happy path: multi-segment plaintext with a short final segment is split, per-segment AEAD encrypted, segment-wise downloaded and incrementally verified, and the top-level ciphertext_digest is recomputed and matches per media-and-blob.md section 3.3.

Streaming AEAD scheme closure: an unknown attachment scheme MUST fail closed with unsupported_attachment_scheme (no fallback decrypt); an envelope carrying both whole-file nonce and chunked nonce_prefix/segment_* fields MUST fail blob.schema.json encrypted_attachment oneOf validation.

Streaming AEAD truncation: a dropped final segment, a last segment whose flag stays 0x00, or segment_count exhausted without last_segment_flag=0x01 MUST be rejected with segment_stream_truncated and buffered plaintext discarded.

calendar.attendees is the single canonical roster: actor ids are unique, the omitted role defaults to required, at most one organizer exists, and roster membership creates no Realm or Circle membership and widens no history access.

One schedule patch derives exactly one notification per receiver over the pre/post roster union filtered by post-state access, mute, DND and push rules; encrypted schedules only produce the profile-defined blind wakeup; RSVP changes derive no schedule notification.

Calendar Strands activate exactly one way: Strand.schema_refs carries ak.schema.calendar_event.v1 and metadata.fields.calendar co-occurs in both directions on the post-patch object, the container self-schema is refused in schema_refs, legacy flat schedule fields and metadata.fields.profile/profile_refs impostors are refused, and writes bind the schema in requirements.schema[].

Nonexistent and ambiguous local times both resolve with the offset in effect before the transition, so a fixed local meeting time does not drift across a DST boundary and the overlap emits exactly one occurrence.

RFC 8984 subset defaults, base start as the first occurrence counted against count, implicit inheritance of base time and weekday components, count/until typing and exclusivity, by_* companion preconditions, and the paginated expansion with its candidate-period scan budget and revision-bound continuation.
Excluded recurrence rules, recurrence overrides, RDATE/EXDATE, per-instance reschedule or cancellation, and the JSCalendar @type discriminator all fail closed instead of being silently ignored.

RSVP admission is capability-based rather than attendee-based, refuses cancelled events, and layers basis checks so that e2ee and plaintext Realms accept the identical canonical set: shape admission rejects without resolving anything, target admission reads only the referenced Events plaintext envelope and pends on dependency_missing, and basis validity is projection-only. It also fails closed above the 128-entry frontier bound and keeps missing, invisible, cross-Realm and non-calendar targets externally indistinguishable.

RSVP derives a typed composite subject from payload event_ref, nullable occurrence, and the explicitly sourced envelope actor_id; causal successors dominate while concurrent mv_register heads remain exposed independently of HLC.

Instance heads override series fallback without unioning them into a false conflict, causal successors dominate independently of arrival order and HLC, missing keys project encrypted_unresolved instead of a fabricated status, and equal decrypted plaintext is not a conflict merely because ciphertexts differ.
RSVP occurrence key canonicalizes recurrence instance local wall-clock start in the event timezone.

The RSVP response branch follows the effective scope encryption floor: plaintext is refused under an e2ee floor, permitted only with the declared rsvp_response data class otherwise, never silently downgraded, and the routing-visible metadata set is disclosed explicitly.

ak.rsvp.set declares one deterministic reducer projection, set(payload.entry): an implementation that omits the registered write, projects an extra target, or derives a value different from the canonical payload entry fails conformance. Those writes are reducer-local output and never producer-selected Event fields.

Identity-affecting schedule edits orphan instance RSVPs and mark series RSVPs needs_reconfirmation, non-calendar updates are not schedule revisions, divergent concurrent heads block RSVP until a resolution Event, and byte-identical concurrent heads settle without picking a winner.

all_day selects the date branch and its negation the whole-second LocalDateTime branch for start, end and recurrence.until; intervals are half-open so end is strictly later than start; UTC timestamps, offsets, bracketed zones and fractional seconds are refused.

Producers canonicalize Link aliases to the canonical Zone before signing, receivers refuse non-canonical signed zones, a schedule-signed tzdb_version outside the executable set fails closed, and a release bump may move derived instants without changing the signed timezone or any local occurrence key.
Same-basis sibling transitions to different states return fsm bottom instead of selecting a winner.
Accepts the three legal first call states and rejects active or terminal first states.
Moderator kick/ban requires ak.call.moderate (call_moderation_unauthorised otherwise); the call moderation effective OR-Set gates token re-issue with call_participant_removed.

P2P calls converge to SFU when participants exceed two, reusing the oldest_membership no-vote session_focus election; mode does not auto-downgrade, and ak.call.summary is gated on a terminal call state (call_summary_invalid otherwise).

Recording ready results MUST carry ak.schema.call_recording_artifact.v1 metadata bound to the recording start event, Arkret blob pipeline, recording exporter label/context, retention policy, deletion audit trigger, and erasure receipt.

Recording retention: audit_lock blocks deletion (legal_hold_active) regardless of retention_expires_at, and ak.call.recording.start cannot enter a capturing state without an atomically persisted consent_confirmed result.
Same-basis replay of the same from/to transition is idempotent and does not create a divergent head.
Terminal call states reject every attempted outgoing transition with call_state_terminal.

Transcription requires ak.call.transcribe (transcription_denied otherwise), and transcript artifacts MUST use the ak.rtc-transcript-key/v1 exporter label with a dedicated Context (transcription_artifact_pipeline_bypassed otherwise).
Covers every legal call lifecycle transition and representative non-terminal illegal transitions.
Profile-declared non-event grant authority permits only exact Realm-admin-to-active-bridge-registration ak.applet.ghost.provision grants and rejects owner shortcuts or binding drift.

Capability materialization copies issuer_principal_server_id exactly from the accepted carrier Event, derives maximum depth plus canonical sorted and deduplicated root identities, and requires each parent subject authority pair to equal the child issuer pair. Producer-supplied derived members and same-DID cross-Principal-Server replay are rejected; missing parents remain dependency-pending and independent reducers produce the same state-root input.

A multi-level authority chain built from one grant shape: each grant records the grant it was issued under in issuer_authority_refs, and revoking an ancestor invalidates its descendants at read time without any cascading write.
Delegation cycle rejection across direct, multi-hop, revoke/redelegate and atomic batch variants.
A fixed authority expiry seal prevents rolling renewal and stops a re-granted authority from widening the window of the refs that cover it.

Grant-ref liveness follows upstream revocation without cascade writes, root refs survive controller transfer but fail after generation reset, and root-control terminal events reject ordinary grant-based authorization.
Reducer-only ak.capability.derived follows the unified issuer-authority rules while retaining Realm-link inheritance behavior and remaining unauthorable by principals.
Direct Conversation participant authority is a profile-scoped non-grant source, survives root generation changes, requires the pair's unique immutable binding, and cannot issue child grants.
Risk-tier freshness matrix fails closed and keeps unknown low-risk pending outcomes local.
Global cross-grant decision merge prevents any allow from bypassing deny, quarantine or review.
Issuer effective-authority and freshness-unknown fail-closed checks for first-issued grants.
Static depends_on_moderation_state requirement rejects missing or false declarations.

Subject-only relinquish needs no revoke grant, rejects non-subjects and root-cell targets, and both revoke and relinquish stay dependency-pending without prewriting tombstones when the target grant is unresolved.

The unified grant form preserves depth, expiry-seal, cycle and constraint inheritance, permits unbounded low/medium-risk multi-hop agent grants, and requires finite expiry for high-risk agent or service grants.
Effective grant validity-window intersection rejects empty windows.
External authority authority Ack issuance, canonical receipt-set assembly, common-window calculation, threshold deduplication, exact replay and decision-chain binding.
Control Proposal Ack deadlines, at most two immutable-horizon signed defers, decision-overdue evidence, and acceptance of a later cryptographically valid Seal.
Realm proposal decision windows are ordered and realizable: decision <= absolute, equality is accepted only with zero defers, and invalid configurations fail before any Realm state write.
cas_register writes on non-initial state require an explicit CBA basis: Control Move preconditions or equivalent DataEvent causal/lattice proof; null-basis blind overwrites fail closed.
bottom=reject control cell recovery accepts only a sealed conflict-recovery Move with valid recovery_capability and pre-conflict state_witness; negative cases pin recovery_witness_* reasons.
open_set concurrent revocation is evaluated against the joined control view; revoked or bottom authorization cells fail closed without a freshness window.
Seal canonical bytes exclude id and notary_signature; verifier recomputes the typed id and signature payload digest from signed top-level fields only.
directory_visibility=realm_members exposes only the Realm-member preview field set and gives non-Realm callers the same locked stub/timing bucket as members-only circles.

Circle lifecycle is evaluated at the Event CBA basis; linear archive uses the revocation freshness window, tombstone and concurrent archive fail closed immediately, and restore never rehabilitates a pre-archive basis.

Hard quota counters use one logical linearizable authority across every service node: a race for the last slot cannot overshoot, idempotent retries count once, unavailable authority fails closed, and calendar-month periods are rejected.

Temporal action gates are neutral for unrelated actions according to effect, while edit/redact windows use the verified target created_at and the fixed verification time/skew to accept inside the deadline and fail closed outside or on missing target time.

Authority-surface coverage for ak.authority.direct_conversation_repair.v1, whose action_allowlist is exactly ak.member.rejoin.own. A self leave -> join ak.member.state under the repair source matches that action and reports it as the matched authority source; joining on behalf of the other participant, carrying a first join, admitting a third participant, presenting ak.member.leave.own under the repair source (daily self-leave belongs to the participant authority) and running rejoin.own backwards as join -> leave all fail closed. Behavioural rejoin vectors that never name the action or the authority source would stay green with an empty allowlist and therefore do not cover this.

The ak.self.contact.read.list projection carries the closed next_prepare_input successor cursor: an accepted row MUST carry it and the five non-authorable contact_state values MUST NOT, its basis_id, version and predecessor_event_ref are copied verbatim into the scope_update and tombstone prepare phases, version is the next Event's version and predecessor_event_ref is the current lineage head rather than that head's predecessor, and a stale cursor is refused with contact_lineage_conflict or contact_scope_stale and MUST be re-read rather than guessed or retried unchanged.

The ak.self.contact.read.list projection carries the complete signed request_receipt on a pending_incoming row, so respond and reject become authorable: the field name is byte-identical to the prepare field that consumes it, it is copied verbatim and never narrowed to a reference, and because it is signed by the peer's source service rather than by the holder's own server the client verifies it independently instead of trusting its server's retelling. pending_outgoing, accepted, rejected, expired and tombstoned rows MUST NOT carry it, a glare pair is structurally never pending_incoming so respond and reject stay forbidden without a new code, and a consumed receipt is refused by prepare with zero writes and MUST be re-read rather than cached or replayed.
KeyPackage upload, entry upload, consume, and revoke signatures use one byte-exact operation-id domain plus typed unsigned-request JCS transcript shared by ordinary devices and Native Agent runtimes.

accepted_device pairing signs a closed target-owned possession attestation under ak.device-authorize-accepted-device-possession-proof-v1 whose only replay boundary is the pairing challenge transcript digest: the approving device and the Account Authority each rebuild it independently, it is the sole authority for hpke_key and algorithms, short-link and to-device share one schema and one domain, transcripts never cross between root_anchored and accepted_device, and the target device fails closed before local assembly when the accepted Event does not match its attestation or the expected principal_id.

document_digest is sha256:lowercase_hex(SHA-256(RFC8785_JCS(normalized DID Document projection))): any raw JSON property reordering keeps the digest identical, changing any controller / verification relationship / service / security-relevant extension property necessarily changes it, and raw response bytes are never carried in document_digest (they use raw_document_digest).

evidence_digest is recomputable from the retained canonical evidence receipt (ak.did.binding_evidence.v1): a proofless method degrades to an empty method_proofs array rather than a placeholder, webvh witness rows are sorted by witness_did with duplicates rejected, any method evidence change changes the digest, and unknown method or proof kinds fail closed.

policy_digest is recomputable from the retained canonical resolver policy snapshot (ak.did.resolver_policy.v1): required core dimensions (accepted_did_methods, fail_mode, trust_roots) plus the profile-closed profile_policy, registered wire tokens only (language-native debug renderings rejected), and flipping any security-relevant field necessarily changes the digest while unknown profiles or fields fail closed.

Byte-exact KAT for the receiver-derived off-wire Direct Conversation binding digest: fixed v1 domain separator, closed normalized binding object, unordered participant and authorization-ref normalization, created_at and Event-context exclusion, and semantic-field mutation separation.

One accepted founding unit per (founder_id, trust_domain_id, pair_key) slot across same-Principal-Server, dual-Principal-Server and founder multi-device concurrency: first valid unit wins, the loser gets direct_conversation_slot_already_committed with zero writes, exact replay returns the byte-identical receipt without advancing accepted_at, the same idempotency key with a different unit is duplicate_conflict, every crash point converges to the same coordinates, and the federation branch reports a missing bounded dependency as a top-level retryable dependency_missing rather than a partial.

The creation_required resolver outcome carries next_founding_input with member names identical to the founding unit submission, exactly one founding_authority_evidence branch, no Event bytes or coordinates, temporarily_unavailable when the material cannot be assembled, and submission-side re-verification that never trusts the echoed copy.

Cross-author replacement repair dispatch: registered self dispatch freezes a byte-identical peer relay outbox; the destination atomically freezes either all current authorized human devices or one current Native-Agent runtime endpoint and enqueues all-or-zero; requester authority is closed device|native_agent and byte-bound to accepted rejoin and KeyPackage signer evidence; repair claims consume only the exact target_keypackage_ref through a closed human-device|native-agent selector; durable Commit/Welcome plus activation remain the only business response.

Caller-authored first-valid founding unit: byte-exact founding_unit_digest KAT over the three ordered Event IDs, realm_id and main_strand_id retyped from the first and third Event IDs, closed self and peer carrier branch shapes, and rejection of server-allocated identifiers, reserved or materializing drafts, coordinator election, reordering, a fourth Event and a carried coordinate field.

The hard cap of sixteen not-yet-active candidate MLS groups under one Direct Conversation active-generation predecessor: the sixteenth candidate MUST be admitted, the seventeenth MUST be refused with the exact registered code mls_generation_proposal_fanout_exceeded at HTTP 409 on both the self and the peer Event submit entry points, the refusal is not rate_limited and carries no retry window, and the pair MUST NOT be quarantined - coordinates, binding, membership, the current active generation and the resolver state all stay unchanged and the refusal writes nothing.
Canonical direct-conversation pair_key KAT over sorted stable subject DIDs and the Realm trust domain, including order-independence and unresolved-pairwise-DID rejection rules.
Direct Conversation Realm profile/discriminator bidirectional schema guard, MLS and closed-join shape, exact-two membership, no-Space policy and main-Strand invariants.

The Direct Conversation resolver reports only server-verifiable send blockers. personal_blocked and history_key_unavailable are absent from the closed wire enum because holder blocklist state is encrypted to holder devices and history key installation is device-private, so a reply carrying either value is a schema_violation; they are carried instead by the closed client-local blocker set, which never appears on any wire surface and never turns the resolver state into suspended. presence_offline and keypackage_empty remain server-verifiable but are returned only to an existing exact-pair participant, and a non-participant probe gets the same opaque failure as a nonexistent pair.

Leave, block, either directional Contact terminal and participant terminal gates suspend the immutable conversation; Consent is not consulted. Recovery reuses the same Realm and main Strand with a new active MLS generation and never automatically redelivers old epoch keys or history secrets.
resolve_agent_selector failure branches for missing, hidden, and unauthorized selectors return the same status, body shape, error class, and timing bucket.
resolve_handle failure branches for missing, hidden, and unauthorized handles return the same status, body shape, error class, and timing bucket.
Canonical JSON object key ordering follows UTF-16 code units for supplementary-plane keys.
Canonical confusable-check test set and callable SDK utility behavior.
ECDSA P-256 (ES256, RFC 6979 deterministic) detached JWS golden vector over the canonical proof binding object, mirroring the ed25519 vector structure for the optional interop signature suite.

ML-DSA-65 (FIPS 204) raw detached signature golden vector over the canonical proof binding object bytes (registry proof_kind raw_detached_signature; keygen from a recorded xi seed, signature published as a recorded value that verifiers only verify).

Executable signature negative family for Ed25519, ES256, and ML-DSA-65: bad or truncated signatures, alg/key-type mismatch, malformed algorithm-specific public keys, and detached-profile confusion; every case MUST be rejected with the recorded error_code.
BLAKE3 KAT over fixed UTF-8 bytes plus wrong-prefix, wrong-length, Realm-suite mismatch, and unknown-suite downgrade rejection cases.

Event Batch Receipt events[] is a canonical set projection sorted by UTF8(canonical_json(item)) with duplicates removed before signing; receivers reject unsorted or duplicate signed wire arrays before digest verification.

Canonical OR-Set dot (ak:event:<event_id>:<write_index>, write_index taken from the registry cell_writes[]) and the or_set_batch_add tag digest encoding, with negative cases for a bare event_id tag and for deriving the third segment from a wire array index.

Hand-written deterministic CBOR bounds: a definite-length array declaring/carrying 65537 items (generator-described, built by the runner) exceeds the v1 cap of 65536 items per array/map and MUST be rejected (reason_code cbor_bounds_invalid) without preallocating from the declared count.

CBOR indefinite-length item (raw bytes bf616101ff, the indefinite-length map {_ "a": 1}) violates RFC 8949 section 4.2 deterministic encoding and MUST be rejected (reason_code cbor_not_deterministic); locks the SDK's existing indefinite-length rejection on the mls_governance_binding decode path.

CBOR capacity bomb: a byte string header declaring 4294967295 bytes with only 4 bytes of remaining input (raw bytes 5affffffffdeadbeef) MUST be rejected (reason_code cbor_bounds_invalid) before any buffer is allocated from the declared length.

Canonical structure depth cap: a JSON object nested 65 levels deep (generator-described, built by the runner; top-level container = depth 1) exceeds the v1 maximum nesting depth of 64 (objects and arrays combined) and MUST be rejected (reason_code structure_depth_exceeded) with bounded recursion; a depth-64 control input MUST be accepted.
Positive and negative wire vectors for the arkret-acct-uri custom JSON string format, including negatives that only the normative profile validator can reject.
Positive and negative wire vectors for the arkret-agent-slug custom JSON string format, including negatives that only the normative profile validator can reject.
Positive and negative wire vectors for the arkret-canonical-handle custom JSON string format, including negatives that only the normative profile validator can reject.
Positive and negative wire vectors for the arkret-content-text custom JSON string format, including negatives that only the normative profile validator can reject.
Positive and negative wire vectors for the arkret-human-identifier custom JSON string format, including negatives that only the normative profile validator can reject.
Positive and negative wire vectors for the arkret-idna-a-label-domain custom JSON string format, including negatives that only the normative profile validator can reject.
Positive and negative wire vectors for the arkret-short-text custom JSON string format, including negatives that only the normative profile validator can reject.
Positive and negative wire vectors for the arkret-single-line-display-text custom JSON string format, including negatives that only the normative profile validator can reject.

Suite-tagged 264-bit complete event_id identity: one explicit active digest-suite wire_code octet plus all 32 octets of the Event's unchanged event_digest preimage result. Covers SHA-256/BLAKE3 bytes, canonical 44-char unpadded Base64URL, code/full-digest recompute-and-compare, unknown/invalid/reserved suite, padding/length rejection, complete-hash collision quarantine, and that the carried ID cannot drive accepted-state side effects before comparison. It also covers encoding.md 6.0.1 one-way construction and self/sibling preimage-reference rejection.

Requires every active reducer-input kind to have a complete machine-readable cell contract and pins exact multi-target atomicity, missing/extra reducer-projection rejection, and data/control plane-cross-write rejection.

ak.realm.alias is the only wire carrier of a Realm alias: declaration / tombstone shapes, the create-time bootstrap follow-up and post-bootstrap seal_basis shapes, head_eq rename, issuer-authority binding, namespace occupancy, disjointness from the handle namespace, cas_register bottom on concurrent distinct declarations, and rejection of alias on the closed Realm object or in a PCR.
Service-level submit_seal admission covers genesis completeness, current device generation, recomputed roots, predecessor notary authority and non-terminal future-clock deferral.

The standard peer dependency resolve operation is a bounded read-only Event/CBA fetch surface with canonical sorted exact typed selectors, complete selector accounting, indistinguishable missing and undisclosable results, atomic limit_exceeded on response-budget overflow, bounded verifiable supersets, strict progress, an eight-round automatic-fetch ceiling, and a fresh-key submit after closure completion.

Each Event selects its Realm reducer from the authenticated CBA governance basis; ordinary Events and federation service bindings carry no reducer identity, unsupported settled profiles fail with profile_unsupported, and an unregistered upgrade target fails closed.

Ordinary dependency gaps are per-item HTTP 200 partial outcomes with non-empty typed missing sets while registered founding units remain zero-write atomic HTTP 409 dependency_missing outcomes; every received response terminates the prior Idempotency-Key and only a no-response byte-identical transport retry reuses it.

Federation push carries one Realm's bounded, receiver-verifiable CbaProofBundle superset rooted at DataEvent seal_ref and Control Event seal_basis leaves on the sole peer Event write rail; receivers reject unreachable bundle objects, resolve Control Events and basis Seals topologically before DataEvents, and never grant same-batch unsealed authority or advance actor frontiers from proof transport.

Federation ingress authentication-failure family (unknown peer / not authorized / target absent) returns indistinguishable responses within one timing bucket per relation.md section 4.5 sampling rules.
Transition Seal positive path recomputes old and new roots under their respective suites.
Transition Seal root, snapshot, suite, downgrade and post-transition negative matrix.

A Direct Conversation Realm takes its effective ak.realm.history_sharing_policy from the ak.profile.direct_conversation_realm.v1 fixed baseline: the generation-0 provisional history key share to the exact peer is released without an accepted policy Event and must not be refused because pre_join_history is deny, archive_node and recovery_service key sources are withheld, and a post-repair rejoin gets no key for the absence window.

A Principal Control Realm takes its effective ak.realm.history_sharing_policy from the ak.profile.principal_control_realm.v1 fixed baseline: restricted visibility is satisfied without an accepted policy Event, the Realm object must not declare the policy, the PCR must not emit the policy Event, release is clamped to the receiving device's ak.device.authorize frontier, and a Collaboration Realm other than a Direct Conversation Realm gets no implied baseline.

Registering an external Organization DID separates resolution, control verification, local registration, Realm relationship and service delegation; being resolvable or referenceable yields no local administrative authority. prepare/ensure is two-phase by decision: the registry issues and remembers a single-use challenge bound to purpose, audience, origin, trust domain, nonce, local_admin_subject and a window of at most 300 seconds, and the control proof binds that beneficiary to block redirection. Challenge consumption atomically records the canonical request digest and outcome, so only a byte-identical retry is idempotent; the same challenge under a different digest fails closed. proof_kind is a closed two-member discriminator over mature DIDs, witness attestation is never a governance quorum, requested scopes MUST match the challenge, and quorum proofs MUST meet the declared threshold. registration_generation reconciles idempotency with terminal revocation: replacement atomically terminates the old current generation and advances a monotonic current pointer, so an old receipt cannot authorize after supersession. Status is the closed triple active/stale/revoked with rotation mapping to stale and DID deactivation forcing revoked, and revoked is terminal against refresh.

Root-committed FoundingDeviceDescriptor, device possession, one-way authorize payload digest binding, ordered atomic create-once PCR genesis unit, extended identity creation transcript, exact replay and mutation rejection.

Identity-creation saga crash/resume, lease fencing, single-use challenge terminal-state separation, exact replay, client echo validation, signed account binding and post-registration did:webvh history verification.

cas_register join is the pure maximal-chain function over set ops carrying from: a sequential governance lifecycle (declaration -> whole-value head_eq tombstone -> re-declaration) joins to the single terminal value instead of bottom; two ops with the same from and different values form two maximal chains and join to bottom; a non-initial op whose from matches no covered value is a dangling supersession and fails closed to bottom; duplicate (value, from) sets are idempotent; supersession binds by value, so ABA reuse is the documented value-CAS semantic and families needing generational distinction embed a monotonic component in the value.
